raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Fixes #57950.

Non-streaming `FunctionGemmaToolParser.tool_call_regex` used `\w+` for the function name, so names like `get-weather` failed to match and the raw control frame was returned as content. Streaming already accepted hyphens via `func_part.split("{")[0]`.

Widen the name group to `[\w-]+` in both alternations so non-streaming matches streaming and OpenAI-legal hyphenated tool names.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py --noconftest` (17 passed)
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched files
- [x] Added non-streaming and streaming regression tests for `get-weather`

The name fix looks right, and `test_hyphenated_tool_name` fails without it.

One question about [`arg_regex`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3e85fd5d5787a5046d2c6654975db9546996328d/vllm/tool_parsers/functiongemma_tool_parser.py#L49): it has the same `\w+`, and it silently cuts hyphenated keys in both modes:

```
<start_function_call>call:search{city:<escape>Paris<escape>,max-results:<escape>5<escape>}<end_function_call>
-> {"city": "Paris", "results": 5}
```

Would you fold `[\w-]+` in there too, or should that be a separate PR?

nit: you kept `[\w-]+` to match streaming, but names like `get.weather` still differ. Streaming emits the call, while non-streaming returns the raw text as content.
